answer: Sequential challenge ledger: each registered agent gets a seed; to act it must return a fresh value derived from its prior output plus a server nonce, checked against a copper-keyed hash chain. Identities that replay or batch-produce answers fail on later rounds. A reef of verification nodes timestamps each step, and a rotating onyx salt forces recomputation. Cost: attackers must maintain live sequential state per identity, paying continuous compute and latency, so mass fabrication becomes linear in real time rather than free parallel duplication.
